---
name: make-sound
description: "Create sound effects and mix audio tracks for a video or other media deliverable."
applications:
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: primary
  - id: moda
    role: fallback
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: none
---

Honor the user's named tool, saved preference or existing native project. Otherwise sound effects are generated through `voyager` (Eleven sound effects) and mixed and delivered with FFmpeg. Music comes from [make-music](../make-music/SKILL.md).

Voyager’s audio engine is not used for sound effects (whooshes, hits, risers, UI clicks, ticks, or a tone or sonic cue under a motion piece or logo sting), voice cleanup, or cutting or fitting a whole existing or generated track; use the bundled FFmpeg or Python audio libraries for cleanup, mixing, fitting and delivery.

## Mix to the destination

Mix in the picture's existing editor: for a .vdaw score see [make-music](../make-music/SKILL.md#score-a-video); for other video audio follow [edit-video](../edit-video/SKILL.md#route). Use FFmpeg when no ready editing route applies. Match explicit user or destination requirements for loudness, peaks, codecs and format.

`voyager media review FILE` reads the result. For a person's quiet recording: see [finish a recording](../voiceover/SKILL.md#finish-a-recording), and review the processed voice stem, not the mix, with the recording as `--audio-source` so a raised noise floor or crushed dynamics are flagged.
To judge how it sounds, use [watch and listen](../make-ai-video/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).

## Deliver

Put the finished mix in the picture's existing editor, following the editing
skill already in use for that video. With none, mux it with FFmpeg, copying the video stream. See [sound and story](../make-ai-video/SKILL.md#generate-check-deliver).

## Sound effects

Eleven sound effects is the default for effects and looping ambience. Stable Audio suits instrumental music and textures; simple UI clicks, ticks and tones can be synthesized in Python/numpy.

For a model the user names or an unusual job, `voyager models list --query "sound" --json` covers the long tail. `voyager models show MODEL --json` answers inputs and limits, `voyager models estimate` answers price, speed and payer, and `voyager models docs MODEL --json` supplies vendor documentation for fal endpoints.

Generate each effect with `eleven-sound` through `voyager`, prompted per its [sound effects section](#sound-effects-elevenlabs-sound-effects-v2-eleven-sound). Simple UI clicks, ticks and tones can be synthesized in plain Python/numpy instead (free), not in the audio engine.

Real recorded effects, foley and ambiences come from Freesound when the user has saved a key in Connectors › Services › Freesound: `voyager freesound search`, then `get`, which saves the HQ preview with a receipt and a `CREDITS` line.

When delivering a cue pack, identify the files and intended cue times; use the requested delivery format.

## Sound effects: ElevenLabs Sound Effects v2 (`eleven-sound`)

- One sound per prompt.
  Write a short sequence in order ("footsteps on gravel, then a metal door opens"); layer anything longer in the mix.
- Follow `payerNote` on `voyager models estimate` for the paying route. Read `voyager models show eleven-sound --json` for route-specific duration limits and loop controls; leave duration unset to let the model choose. Use a loop for beds.
- Where the model card exposes `prompt_influence`, raise it for a specific hit; keep it low for varied takes.
- Inspect the returned file and convert to 48 kHz WAV before mixing; the model card lists output formats and loop restrictions.

## Stable Audio 2.5

Always set `seconds_total`; check its default and limits with `voyager models show fal-ai/stable-audio-25/text-to-audio --json`.

## Asset Sources

`voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` and
`voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` cover Poly Haven, ambientCG and Kenney
(CC0), game-icons.net and Incompetech; downloads land in `assets/<source>/<id>/` with a receipt
and a `CREDITS` line. An asset you get another way gets the same by hand: `<asset-id>.json`
beside its files (`source`, `id`, `title`, `url`, `authors`, `license`, `licenseUrl`,
`attribution`, `acquiredAt`, `files`) and a `CREDITS` line (title, author, source URL, licence).

- Tell users Poly Haven assets come from Poly Haven. Kenney search matches pack names only.
- game-icons.net is CC BY 3.0, credited per icon author; Incompetech is CC BY 4.0 with Kevin
  MacLeod's credit text, single tracks only.
- Lospec palettes: `https://lospec.com/palette-list/<slug>.json`; credit "<palette> by <author>
  (Lospec)", taking the author from the page when the JSON's is empty.
- Godot Asset Library (plugins and scripts, not art):
  `godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset?filter=…&godot_version=4.3` (nothing without
  `godot_version`); `cost` is the licence, `/asset/<id>` gives `download_url`.
- OpenGameArt has no API: search pages only, 10 s crawl delay, `/search/` disallowed; licences
  per page.
- Mixamo and itch.io: the user downloads in their own browser (Mixamo's terms forbid other
  access, and its assets aren't redistributable raw; itch.io has no public API).

## Start audio late in FFmpeg

To start audio late in raw FFmpeg, insert silent samples with
  `adelay=delays=9500:all=1` (milliseconds; an `S` suffix means samples;
  without `all=1` only the first channel moves). Before
  delivering, check the decoded length and where the leading silence ends
  (`silencedetect=n=-50dB:d=0.1`).
